findings.summary: The restored per-block table lists shares of 99.15%, 67.48%, 31.41% and 17.20% (215.24% in total) with no cue that the stubs nest, i.e. that stubbing the value path also removes the gradient and Hessian bodies that the narrower stubs remove. A reader who adds the column reads an impossible total, and the same presentation was already noted against the figure at ccc984ff0.

The erased-flag diagnostic swaps its two format arguments: the template names the block first and the flag second, while the tuple passes block['erased'] then block['block']. Reproduced against a receipt whose residual-tangents lowered_bytes is one byte short of control: the refusal prints 'True: erased flag residual-tangents disagrees with lowered bytes 6088066', naming the boolean as the block and the block as the flag. The refusal itself (exit 1) is correct; only the message a reader debugs from is wrong.

check_figure compares only text found in the SVG — arm bar labels, two span labels, the word 'erased' and the absence of #cc0000 — so a figure whose bar lengths were redrawn from other numbers while its labels stayed would pass, although the module docstring at line 9 claims a figure drawn from other data fails here. The figure's geometry is what carries the comparison; only its text is guarded.

Nothing invokes the checker: no test imports or runs it, scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit runs only nova.database.scripts relativize --check, and no suite entry names it, so the record can drift from the committed receipt and only a reader who remembers to run the script learns of it. The worker demonstrated the four refusals by hand and the durability gate log records them, but the guard is manual.
